title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Freedom in the World 2022 Country Report
claim: Freedom House says opposition parties and civil society viewed Tshisekedi's 2021 CENI reform as an attempt to keep the electoral body under presidential control, and it says the CENI and Constitutional Court lacked independence.
source_confidence_reason: Major annual country report from a well-established monitor, with direct institutional findings and contemporaneous context.
period_fit: Near-period country assessment covering the 2021-2022 transition into the target year.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributes the CENI reform and control concerns to Tshisekedi's administration.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes some opposition members were released from prison and some exiled politicians returned.

title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo
claim: The report says the state of siege in North Kivu and Ituri transferred powers from civilian to military authorities, restricted rights, extended military-court jurisdiction, and suspended immunity for elected officials.
source_confidence_reason: Official annual human-rights report with explicit DRC-specific findings and clear period coverage.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributes the state-of-siege framework to Tshisekedi's presidency and its effects to his administration.
contrary_evidence: The report also says the government took some steps to investigate and punish abuses, though impunity remained widespread.

title: DRC: One year on, 'State of Siege' used as a tool to crush dissent
claim: Amnesty says the state of siege was used to crush dissent, with activists arbitrarily detained, protesters attacked, and critics silenced in North Kivu and Ituri.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous NGO briefing with specific cases, named provinces, and direct attribution of abuses.
period_fit: Target-year adjacent evidence within the same 2022 governance environment.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributes the restrictive emergency regime to President Tshisekedi and his security authorities.
contrary_evidence: Amnesty notes the government said the measure was meant to protect civilians and fight armed groups.

title: Pre-election tension in DRC fuels attacks on reporters covering politics
claim: RSF says at least seven journalists were harassed or attacked in Kinshasa and Kananga in July 2022, and it warns that the political climate around Tshisekedi's bid for another term was endangering media work.
source_confidence_reason: Specialized press-freedom monitor with concrete contemporaneous reporting, though the page date is not fully explicit in the excerpt.
period_fit: Directly in the target year and tied to the pre-election environment.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: the article ties the climate to Tshisekedi's re-election drive and the authorities' duty to protect media.
contrary_evidence: The piece frames the issue as a broader political tension, not only a direct order from the presidency.

title: Two Congolese journalists detained for 5 months after covering a protest
claim: CPJ says Patrick Lola and Christian Bofaya were held for more than five months after covering a protest, and that the arrests were politically motivated.
source_confidence_reason: Specialized press-freedom monitor with named journalists, dates, and direct legal-process details.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the article links the detentions to protest coverage critical of local authorities in Tshisekedi's DRC.
contrary_evidence: The arrests were carried out by provincial authorities, so the immediate attribution is local rather than purely presidential.

title: Congolese journalists Patrick Lola and Christian Bofaya unable to pay bail, denied release
claim: CPJ says the two journalists remained detained because they could not pay bail of 2 million Congolese francs each after being arrested while covering a political protest.
source_confidence_reason: Specialized monitor with precise dates, bail amount, and detention outcome based on court documents and lawyer testimony.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to ruler responsibility because the detention flowed through the Congolese court and police system under Tshisekedi's administration.
contrary_evidence: The court formally set bail, so the abuse here is in the scale and consequence of the bail, not the absence of any judicial process.

title: Three Congolese radio journalists stripped, beaten by intelligence agents
claim: CPJ says the head of the National Intelligence Agency in Tshuapa summoned three journalists after a broadcast criticizing alleged surveillance of students, then ordered them stripped and beaten.
source_confidence_reason: Detailed contemporaneous report with named agency officials, journalists, and a specific broadcast trigger.
ruler_attribution: Directly implicates a state intelligence service operating under the national government.
contrary_evidence: The abuse was provincial and agency-specific, not a formal national media policy statement.

title: Congolese journalist Dimanche Kamate arrested, detained over broadcast about Rwanda, protests
claim: CPJ says national police arrested and detained Dimanche Kamate for several hours after a broadcast that included civil-society commentary on Rwanda and protests.
source_confidence_reason: Specific contemporaneous case with named journalist, police action, and broadcast content.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to state policing and media control under Tshisekedi's government.
contrary_evidence: The detention was temporary, so it shows intimidation more than long-term imprisonment.

title: DRC journalist Tatiana Osango sexually assaulted, two other journalists attacked by police in separate incident
claim: CPJ says an opposition politicians' supporters sexually assaulted Tatiana Osango while she was covering a meeting, and police separately beat two other journalists covering a protest in Kinshasa.
source_confidence_reason: Strong contemporaneous reporting with named victims, perpetrators, dates, and supporting local press-freedom references.
ruler_attribution: The police attack is directly attributable to state actors; the opposition-supporter assault shows a wider hostile political environment the state failed to control.
contrary_evidence: One assault was by opposition supporters rather than state authorities, so it is not all ruler-attributable.

title: Armed men in military uniforms beat, threaten lives of Congolese journalists Parfait Katoto and Picard Luhavo
claim: CPJ reports that armed men dressed in Congolese military uniforms forcibly entered two journalists' homes in Ituri, beat them, and threatened their lives.
source_confidence_reason: Specific named victims, dates, and modus operandi, with direct local corroboration in the article.
ruler_attribution: Strongly relevant because the attackers wore military-style uniforms in a province under national security control.
contrary_evidence: The article does not prove the attackers were official soldiers, only that they wore uniforms resembling them.

title: Armed men in military uniforms raid Congolese broadcaster, beat technician, and seize equipment, forcing radio station off air
claim: CPJ says four armed men in military-style uniforms raided Radio Evanglique Butembo-Oicha, beat a technician, seized equipment, and forced the station off air.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous press-freedom report with named station, place, and concrete abuses.
ruler_attribution: Relevant to state responsibility because the attackers presented themselves as military personnel in a security-sensitive area.
contrary_evidence: The attackers were not conclusively identified as official army personnel in the article.

title: Congolese journalists face death threats as M23 rebels advance, flee for safety
claim: CPJ says at least 23 journalists fled to MONUSCO in late October 2022 after the M23 takeover and threats to kill local journalists.
source_confidence_reason: Strong contemporaneous reporting with a precise count of displaced journalists and a clear threat context.
ruler_attribution: Mostly indirect, because the immediate threat came from M23 rather than the presidency, but it shows the broader political-freedom environment Tshisekedi governed.
contrary_evidence: The immediate perpetrators were a rebel group, so the article is more about inherited insecurity than direct presidential repression.

title: RDC: Jean Marc Kabund arrete
claim: Actualite.cd reports that Jean-Marc Kabund was arrested before his parliamentary immunity was lifted and sent to Makala after remarks deemed insulting to the president.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting with named lawyer, police reference, and direct procedural detail.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant because Kabund was a former presidential ally turned opposition figure arrested after attacking Tshisekedi publicly.
contrary_evidence: The article presents the arrest through the justice process, so it does not by itself prove a presidential order.

title: RDC: Felix Tshisekedi prend acte du serment de trois nouveaux juges de la Cour constitutionnelle
claim: Actualite.cd reports that Tshisekedi presided over the swearing-in of three new Constitutional Court judges who replaced sitting judges, placing the presidency at the center of court staffing.
source_confidence_reason: Local contemporaneous reporting on a formal judicial appointment ceremony, with direct quotations from the oath.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi's formal role in judicial appointments.
contrary_evidence: The article does not show whether the appointments were independently selected or politically motivated in practice.

title: Kinshasa : la police disperse la marche des partisans du parti de Kabund
claim: Radio Okapi says police dispersed a march by supporters of Kabund's party in Kinshasa even though organizers said they had notified authorities in advance.
source_confidence_reason: Local broadcaster with direct reporting on police action, organizer complaint, and the march's stated purpose.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to the government's tolerance of opposition mobilization in Tshisekedi's capital.
contrary_evidence: Police said the march had not been authorized, so the state gave a legality-based justification.

title: Jean-Marc Kabund: 'Le regime Tshisekedi a lamentablement echoue'
claim: Radio Okapi quotes Kabund publicly denouncing Tshisekedi's regime as a failure and saying tribalism and regionalism had returned.
source_confidence_reason: Direct local quotation from a prominent opposition figure in a contemporaneous radio report.
period_fit: Directly in the target year, but this is opposition speech rather than ruler conduct.
ruler_attribution: Indirect only: it shows opposition criticism and the broader political atmosphere around Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: This item is a statement by the opposition, not an act by Tshisekedi himself.

title: Congo arrests opposition leader Kabund
claim: Reuters reports that Jean-Marc Kabund was arrested after falling out with Tshisekedi, and says the episode highlighted emerging fault lines in the ruling coalition.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting syndicated by a mainstream outlet, with named actor, date, and clear political context.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to the president's treatment of a former close ally turned opposition leader.
contrary_evidence: The story does not establish a direct presidential instruction for the arrest.

title: Top Congo presidential adviser resigns after allegedly requesting bribe on tape
claim: Reuters says a top Tshisekedi adviser resigned after an alleged bribe tape, and the president's office framed the case as evidence that people in the presidency would face consequences for violating the law.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a concrete corruption case with a presidential response and named adviser.
ruler_attribution: Directly concerns the president's inner circle and how Tshisekedi handled an integrity scandal.
contrary_evidence: This is a corruption/accountability case, not direct proof of political liberalization or repression.

title: Human Rights Documents - DRC report listing
claim: OHCHR's DRC document index lists A/HRC/51/61, the 10 August 2022 report on the human rights situation and UNJHRO activities in the DRC, covering 1 June 2021 to 31 May 2022.
source_confidence_reason: This is source metadata rather than substantive findings, but it is an official UN index confirming the report's existence and period coverage.
period_fit: Period-adjacent context, not direct evidence on its own.
ruler_attribution: Indirect only; it identifies an official UN report relevant to the same governance period.
contrary_evidence: The listing itself contains no substantive findings.

title: Protesters in Congo call for the release of political prisoners
claim: AP says protesters accused Tshisekedi of trying to muzzle opponents and silence dissenting voices while demanding the release of Kabund, Mukebayi, and Kikuni.
source_confidence_reason: Major wire report with named protest organizers and direct quotation, but published after the target year.
period_fit: Post-period confirmation of a continuing repression pattern, not direct 2022 evidence.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to the longer Tshisekedi trajectory.
contrary_evidence: This article is outside the 2022 target period, so it should not be used as direct evidence for the target year.

title: DR Congo: Martial Law Brings Crackdown in East
claim: HRW says the military and police curtailed freedom of expression, used lethal force against peaceful demonstrations, and arbitrarily detained and prosecuted activists, journalists, and political opposition members in North Kivu and Ituri under martial law declared by Tshisekedi's administration.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights report with explicit attribution to Tshisekedi's administration and concrete examples of coercive repression.
period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target period and the same emergency regime that continued through 2022.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Tshisekedi's administration, which declared and maintained the martial law framework.
contrary_evidence: The administration said the measure was meant to address insecurity and protect civilians.

title: National convention’s decisions could herald new era for journalists in DRC
claim: RSF says Tshisekedi presided over a January 2022 media convention, reiterated his desire to guarantee journalist safety through a dedicated alert mechanism, and the convention recommended abolishing prison sentences for press offences and imposing a moratorium on arrests of journalists.
source_confidence_reason: Direct RSF report with clear date, named presidential role, and specific reform proposals for the press environment.
period_fit: Directly in the target year and aimed at reforms implemented during 2022.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Tshisekedi, who presided over the convention and publicly endorsed the reforms.
contrary_evidence: RSF frames the reforms as proposals and encouragement, not proof of implemented legal change during 2022.

title: Two DRC radio stations suspended, transmitters seized over broadcasts criticizing politicians
claim: CPJ reports that on October 25, 2022, Sankuru administrator Bono Emakitshi suspended Radio Losanganya and Radio Grand Tam-tam and ordered their transmitters seized over broadcasts critical of politicians.
source_confidence_reason: Named officials, dated directive, specific outlets, and a clear press-freedom restriction documented by CPJ.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to ruler responsibility because it reflects state-level censorship under Tshisekedi's administration.
contrary_evidence: The immediate action came from a provincial administrator, not a presidential decree.

title: DRC journalist Olivier Makambu jailed over broadcast following defamation complaint
claim: CPJ says police arrested journalist Olivier Makambu after a defamation complaint over a broadcast about interference in a local succession dispute, and CPJ warned that repeated arrests show the press is not safe under Felix Tshisekedi's presidency.
source_confidence_reason: Specific case report with arrest date, legal basis, and explicit press-freedom assessment from CPJ.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to state treatment of journalists under Tshisekedi's presidency, even though the complaint originated locally.
contrary_evidence: The arrest followed a formal complaint and warrant process, so the abuse is legal harassment rather than purely extrajudicial detention.

title: French journalist Sonia Rolley expelled from DRC, denied accreditation
claim: CPJ says DRC immigration authorities summoned and expelled Reuters journalist Sonia Rolley after her accreditation was not approved, and CPJ described it as further evidence of deteriorating press freedom.
source_confidence_reason: Clear named case with direct attribution to a state agency and corroboration from Reuters and RFI cited in the article.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to the Tshisekedi administration because the expulsion was carried out by a national immigration authority overseeing press access.
contrary_evidence: The government described the decision as administrative rather than a press-freedom action.

title: Congo’s Indigenous Rights Bill Stalls
claim: HRW notes that on November 16, 2022, President Felix Tshisekedi signed the new law on the Protection and Promotion of the Rights of Indigenous Pygmy Peoples, after the bill had awaited his signature.
source_confidence_reason: Direct HRW update with a precise signature date and a rights-expansion law aimed at an excluded group.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Tshisekedi's personal signature of the law.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes the bill had stalled for months before the signature, so the positive step was delayed.

title: Compte rendu de la soixante-deuxième réunion du Conseil des Ministres
publisher: Présidence de la République Démocratique du Congo
claim: The presidential council report says Tshisekedi praised the promulgation of the law on persons living with disabilities, called it the first such framework in the DRC, and ordered the government to finalize implementing regulations so the protection would be effective.
source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential record of the meeting, with direct statements by Tshisekedi and concrete implementation instructions.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi as head of state and source of the instruction.
contrary_evidence: The text shows a promise and implementation directive, not proof that the law was already fully effective in 2022.

title: Congo schedules presidential elections for Dec 2023
claim: Reuters reported that Congo said it would hold presidential and parliamentary elections on December 20, 2023, that the government pledged to stick to the timetable, and that the spokesman said there was no question of negotiating constitutional deadlines; the report also notes presidents are limited to two terms under Congolese law.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire story carried by Euronews with a precise date, direct quotations, and explicit term-limit framing.
period_fit: Late-2022 evidence about 2023 electoral planning and constitutional timing within the target year.
ruler_attribution: Attributed to the government under Tshisekedi, through the spokesman's public commitment to respect deadlines.
contrary_evidence: This is a pledge about future elections rather than proof of completed clean transfers or non-interference in practice.

title: RDC : La CENI publie le calendrier électoral du cycle 2022-2027
claim: Radio Okapi reports that CENI published the 2022-2027 electoral calendar, with voter registration starting on December 24, 2022, the presidential election set for December 20, 2023, and CENI saying delay was not in its vocabulary.
source_confidence_reason: Direct local reporting on the election body's public announcement with precise dates and a clear quotation about delay.
period_fit: Directly in the target year and the opening of the next electoral cycle.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but important: it reflects the electoral timetable under Tshisekedi's administration and the election body's public posture.
contrary_evidence: The article reports CENI's statement, so it does not itself verify later implementation.

title: Several journalists detained, prosecuted - Civicus Monitor
claim: Civicus says JED documented at least 124 press freedom violations in 2022 in the DRC, including 37 arrests, 18 physical assaults, 17 bans on radio stations or programmes, 2 abductions, and 1 killing, and it quotes JED describing press freedom under Tshisekedi as fragile and worsening.
source_confidence_reason: Secondary rights-monitor summary of a national watchdog report with concrete counts and a direct quotation, though it is not the original report itself.
ruler_attribution: Broadly relevant to the Tshisekedi administration because the report describes the national press environment during his tenure.
contrary_evidence: The figures mix state, local, and non-state abuses, so not every incident is directly presidentially ordered.

title: RDC : environ 124 cas d’atteintes à la liberté de la presse recensés en 10 mois
claim: JED said it recorded about 124 press-freedom violations in the DRC between January and October 2022, including 37 arrests, 18 assaults, 2 kidnappings, 1 killing, and 17 bans on media or programs.
source_confidence_reason: Local reporting on a national watchdog's annual tally with concrete counts and a dated 2022 period.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the violations describe the media environment under Tshisekedi's administration.
contrary_evidence: The tally aggregates abuses by multiple perpetrators, so not every violation is directly presidentially ordered.

title: Elections in the Era of Tshisekedi: A bad start?
publisher: Center on International Cooperation, New York University
claim: The report says that with 14 months left before the next elections, the electoral calendar was still pending, distrust in CENI remained, and controversial reappointments to the Constitutional Court reinforced the lack of trust; it also says political control persisted over CENI and the Constitutional Court.
source_confidence_reason: Research report from a Congo-focused academic center, directly discussing electoral institutions and published in the target year.
period_fit: Directly in the target year and about the next electoral cycle under Tshisekedi.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong institutional attribution to Tshisekedi's era and the electoral bodies operating under his administration.
contrary_evidence: The report is an analytic assessment, not direct proof of a presidential order.

title: RDC : GEC et Ebuteli alertent sur « un spectre de glissement du calendrier électoral »
claim: Radio Okapi reports that GEC and Ebuteli warned that the electoral calendar was still pending, that trust in CENI remained weak, and that political control persisted over CENI and the Constitutional Court, raising a risk of slippage beyond constitutional deadlines.
source_confidence_reason: Local coverage of a Congo-focused research report with explicit quotes and direct 2022 timing.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Tshisekedi because the critique targets the electoral institutions shaping his succession environment.
contrary_evidence: This is a warning about process risk, not proof that deadlines were actually missed in 2022.

title: RDC : La CENI publie le calendrier électoral du cycle 2022-2027
claim: CENI published the 2022-2027 electoral calendar on 26 November 2022, setting presidential, legislative, provincial, and communal elections for 20 December 2023 and saying that slippage was not in its vocabulary.
source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting on the election body's public timetable and a concrete quotation about respecting the schedule.
period_fit: Directly in the target year and directly relevant to the next electoral cycle.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant because the timetable was set under Tshisekedi's administration and his government publicly backed it.
contrary_evidence: This records a plan and pledge, not verified completion of a free contest or transfer.

title: Congo voter registration marred by early kit shortages
claim: Reuters reported that the opening of voter registration was marred by long lines, undersupplied stations, lack of staff and material, and shortages of registration kits, with only 6,900 of more than 11,000 kits delivered for the first phase.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters dispatch with specific observations, quantities, and contemporaneous reporting from the opening of registration.
period_fit: Directly at the end of the target year and at the start of the election cycle.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Tshisekedi's administration because it concerns the state-run election process he was expected to inherit into his reelection bid.
contrary_evidence: The article frames the problem as logistical and resource-related as well as political.

title: Le Président Félix Tshisekedi pour la mise en œuvre des instruments juridiques portant protection des droits des PVH
claim: ACP reports that Tshisekedi, in a 15 July 2022 Council of Ministers communication, praised the new disability law, called it the first such framework in the DRC, and ordered the government to prepare a timetable to make it effective.
source_confidence_reason: Primary government source quoting the president's own communication, with concrete implementation instructions.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi as the president issuing the instruction and framing the reform.
contrary_evidence: The source shows a directive and implementation plan, not proof of full execution in 2022.

title: CENCO-ECC : Planification d’une mission d'observation électorale citoyenne
claim: ACP says CENCO and ECC planned a citizen election-observation mission, asked CENI for accreditation of nearly 600 observers, and CENI gave them election maps, the law, application measures, and voter-registration documents.
source_confidence_reason: Primary local report on a concrete interaction between civil-society observers and the election body.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Tshisekedi because it reflects how open the electoral process was to independent monitoring under his administration.
contrary_evidence: This shows procedural access, not that the process itself was fully fair.

title: Le Président Félix Tshisekedi pour la mise en œuvre des instruments juridiques portant protection des droits des PVH
claim: ACP reports that Tshisekedi called for implementing the new disability-rights law and that the government was tasked with producing a work timetable and related structural measures by the next cabinet meeting.
source_confidence_reason: Primary government report with direct presidential communication and a specific implementation order.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi's formal direction to the government.
contrary_evidence: The article is about implementation planning, not demonstrated outcomes for disabled citizens in 2022.

title: Fonction publique : J-P Lihau signe l'arrêté portant création du Secrétariat général du ministère des Personnes vivant avec handicap
claim: Actu30 reports that the government created a dedicated secretariat-general for the ministry for persons living with disabilities, and officials described it as the materialization of Tshisekedi's inclusion vision.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting on an administrative reform tied to the presidency and disability inclusion.
ruler_attribution: Attributed to Tshisekedi's political vision and the government's implementation of that vision.
contrary_evidence: The reform is administrative and symbolic as well as substantive, so it does not by itself prove broader equality outcomes.

title: Reconnaissance des droits des peuples autochtones pygmées : une victoire historique en RDC
publisher: Agir ensemble pour les droits humains
claim: The organization says the law protecting and promoting indigenous Pygmy rights was passed by Parliament on 11 June 2022, sent to President Tshisekedi, promulgated on 15 July 2022, and published on 14 November 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Rights-organization statement with exact dates for parliamentary passage, presidential promulgation, and publication.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi because the source states he promulgated the law.
contrary_evidence: The source emphasizes a long advocacy process, so the reform was overdue rather than a newly initiated opening.

title: Réforme de la justice : près de 80 hauts magistrats ont prêté serment devant le Président de la République
publisher: Présidence de la République Démocratique du Congo
claim: The presidential office says nearly 80 senior magistrates of the ordinary and administrative judiciary swore their oath before Tshisekedi on 31 August 2022, and it framed the ceremony as part of his effort to continue reforms and consolidate the rule of law.
source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential record of a formal judicial reform ceremony, though naturally self-presenting.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi as the head of state presiding over and framing the reform.
contrary_evidence: The source is presidential and self-justifying, so independent corroboration would strengthen the claim.
